subject: Contract assurance bakeoff: defining SOC 2 / pen test evidence pipeline
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@gatewayhealth.com>, procurement@gatewayhealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Contract assurance bakeoff: defining SOC 2 / pen test evidence pipeline

Hi Elena / Gateway Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I wanted to start a single thread to land the operational approach we discussed for the MSA + Order Form redlines where security exhibit language (SOC 2, pen test, inspection windows, evidence cadence) is concerned. Goal is to create a minimal, repeatable "assurance pipeline" for pilot customers that balances auditability with minimal ops overhead.

Proposed immediate asks:
- Confirm: Gateway expects SOC 2 Type II report quarterly upload (or only on renewal)?
- Pen test window: do you require an on-demand penetration test access clause, or is a scheduled 30-day notice acceptable?
- Evidence cadence: we propose a two-tier cadence: (1) "baseline" automated telemetry & artifacts monthly; (2) "inspection" evidence bundle (sampled artifacts + interviews) quarterly. Will that meet your procurement requirements?
- Ownership: who on your side will own evidence intake (security@gatewayhealth.com?) and who will own procurement acceptance?

I've attached an initial redline (draft_orderform_redline_v3.pdf) and a simple evidence matrix (evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx) showing the artifacts we can deliver automatically vs. those requiring a manual handback.

If useful we can set a short working session tomorrow to walk the matrix and identify any fatal asks that require legal escalation. Proposed 30-minute window: 2026-11-30 10:00-10:30 PT (attached calendar).

Thanks — looking to keep this lightweight and actionable.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Manager, Assurance Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@gatewayhealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, procurement@gatewayhealth.com
Cc: security@gatewayhealth.com (Rajesh Kumar)
Date: 2026-11-29T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Contract assurance bakeoff: defining SOC 2 / pen test evidence pipeline

Hi Ava —

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick answers from procurement/security POV so we can triage:
- SOC 2: for Phase 1 (pilot) Gateway will accept a SOC 2 Type II report within 90 days of go-live; renewal customers require the most recent 12-month report. For large PHI workloads we may request report-backed attestation earlier.
- Pen test: Gateway security is happy with a scheduled 30-day notice for production penetration testing; however for high-risk integrations we reserve the right to request an expedited window with 7-day notice. We will mark which APIs are in the high-risk set in the inventory.
- Evidence cadence: monthly automated artifacts + quarterly inspection bundle sounds reasonable. We need an SLA on the manual bundle turnaround (we typically ask for 5 business days once requested).

Ownership: security@gatewayhealth.com owns intake and can coordinate with procurement for acceptance.

I'll review the redline and matrix; Rajesh will comment on the evidence matrix about sensitive artifact redaction controls.

— Elena
Director, Strategic Procurement
Gateway Health

Date: 2026-11-29T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Contract assurance bakeoff: defining SOC 2 / pen test evidence pipeline

Ava / Elena —

Couple of quick security notes after a skim of the matrix:
- Redaction: any logs or telemetry that could include PHI must be redacted centrally before handback. We need a statement in the exhibit that Redwood will provide a redacted sample and a redaction process description.
- Sampling bands: our default is 10% sampling for access logs and 100% for admin actions. Can you confirm Redwood can produce indexed, time-bound slices (ISO timestamps) to facilitate forensic review?
- Pen test scope: please ensure that the Order Form explicitly lists the API endpoints in scope or refers to an attachable inventory that can be updated without amending the MSA.

I'll add line comments in the draft but flagged items above that are likely to drive legal redlines.

— Rajesh
Head of InfoSec
Gateway Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@gatewayhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Contract assurance bakeoff: defining SOC 2 / pen test evidence pipeline

Thanks — looping in legal observations and proposed short-form redlines to avoid a prolonged redline sprint. High-level suggestions:
1) SOC 2 timing: change wording to "Redwood will provide Client with a SOC 2 Type II report covering the most recent 12-month period within 90 days of go-live for pilots, and thereafter upon each annual renewal." Keeps expectations bounded and avoids quarterly upload obligations.
2) Pen test notice: accept 30-day notice as baseline; add clause that Gateway may request expedited access with written justification limited to specific integrations. Redwood retains right to require a scoped staging environment for high-risk tests.
3) Evidence turnaround SLA: propose 7 business days for the initial tranche, 5 business days for subsequent recurring requests after the first quarter. This gives us time to coordinate engineering handback.
4) Inventory reference: include an "Exhibit B: In-scope Inventory" that is referenced by the Order Form and may be updated by written notice (email) without re-executing the MSA.

I'll attach a short redline that implements the above and calls out where we will provide automated exports vs. manual documents. If Gateway needs a stricter sampling policy (e.g., 100% admin actions), we'll flag that as a billable professional services request in the order form.

[Attachment: draft_orderform_redline_v3.pdf (updated with legal comments)]

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@gatewayhealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, security@gatewayhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-30T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Contract assurance bakeoff: defining SOC 2 / pen test evidence pipeline

Thanks all — quick technical commitment from Redwood's side:
- Automated artifacts: we can provide monthly exports for config snapshots, user/admin activity logs (with redaction pipeline) and model version manifests. These will be delivered to a pre-agreed S3 bucket or secure Drive link.
- Indexed slices: we confirm we can produce ISO8601 time-bounded slices and provide a CSV index to speed forensic lookups.
- Pen test staging: we can preferentially provide a scoped staging environment for high-risk tests; if test scheduled in production, Redwood will require a rolling feature-flag window to limit blast radius.

Next steps: Ava will update the evidence matrix to map each artifact to the delivery mechanism + expected turnaround SLA. Laura will finalize the short-form redline for the order form. Elena / Rajesh to confirm whether expedited pen tests will be requested for any specific APIs (please list by EOD Monday).

— Karthik
Dir, Applied ML Ops (Redwood)
